title: Coherence of compact-support coefficient comparisons and common-stage morphisms
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient fields inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings, uniformizers and finite quotients as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a field $F$ write $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}=\lim_n B_{F,n}$ and $B_{F,n}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $s$, with the coefficient universes of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $H_F=\mathcal L_s^F\mathcal R_s^F$, with actual unit $u^F$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], normalized by [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model]. On the full derived-complete subcategory [def-weil-derived-complete] write $v^F=(u^F)^{-1}$, using [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus].

For each finite $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the raw rational category $\mathcal A_E=D^b_c(s,E)$ and the completed coefficient transitions $S_{L/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with canonical scalar associators $a_{M,L,E}:S_{M/L}S_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{M/E}$ [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Use the rationalized quotient-cone comparisons $\beta_{L/E}:S_{L/E}H_E^{\mathrm{rat}}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L^{\mathrm{rat}}S_{L/E}$ and actual components $v_{E,C}$, $u_{E,C}$ of [lem-pod-reconstruction-raw-rational-naturality]; their integral maps are those of [lem-pod-completion-unit-scalar-intertwining].

The specified compact-support coefficient comparisons are precisely these $\beta$, after the strict identity-tower identifications. They satisfy the identity-extension equation (under the canonical scalar unit identifications) and the following equation of natural transformations for all $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$:
$$ H_M^{\mathrm{rat}}(a_C)\,\beta_{M/L,S_{L/E}C}\,S_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,C})=\beta_{M/E,C}\,a_{H_E^{\mathrm{rat}}C}. $$
In particular this supplies the comparison between $H_E^{\mathrm{rat}}(C)$ extended to a common field and $H_F^{\mathrm{rat}}(S_{F/E}C)$, including its coherence, for the actual compact-support functors.

On the literal common-stage category $\mathcal A=D^b_c(s,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the formulas
$$ \mathcal H(E,C)=(E,H_E^{\mathrm{rat}}C),\qquad \mathcal H[F,h]=[F,\beta_{F/L,D}^{-1}\,H_F^{\mathrm{rat}}(h)\,\beta_{F/E,C}] $$
for $h:S_{F/E}C\to S_{F/L}D$ define the identity compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. This formula is independent of representatives and common fields, and respects identities and composites. The components $[E,v_{E,C}]:\mathcal H(E,C)\to(E,C)$ are a natural isomorphism with inverse $[E,u_{E,C}]$. More explicitly, at any common field $F$ the naturality equation is the transport, by the displayed $\beta$, of
$$ v_{F,S_{F/L}D}\,H_F^{\mathrm{rat}}(h)=h\,v_{F,S_{F/E}C}. $$
It is preserved by every further coefficient extension. No conservativity of finite projections or choice of a preferred common field is assumed.

source.place: First sentence: actual identity-compact-support comparisons and their normalization.

proof.text: For $E=L$ let $e:S_{E/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be the canonical scalar unit. Naturality of $v_E$ at $e_C$ gives $v_{E,C}H_E(e_C)=e_Cv_{E,S_{E/E}C}$; naturality of $e$ at $v_{E,C}$ gives $e_CS_{E/E}(v_{E,C})=v_{E,C}e_{H_EC}$. Insert Step 1 between these equations and cancel $v_{E,C}$ to obtain $H_E(e_C)\beta_{E/E,C}=e_{H_EC}$. This is precisely the identity-extension equation under the unit identifications.

For $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$, abbreviate $T=S_{L/E}$, $U=S_{M/L}$, $V=S_{M/E}$ and $a:UT\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. Postcompose the proposed associator equation with $v_{M,VC}$. On its left, naturality of $v_M$ and Step 1 give successively
$$v_{M,VC}H_M(a_C)\beta_{M/L,TC}U(\beta_{L/E,C})=a_Cv_{M,UTC}\beta_{M/L,TC}U(\beta_{L/E,C})=a_CUT(v_{E,C}).$$
On its right Step 1 and naturality of the specified scalar associator give
$$v_{M,VC}\beta_{M/E,C}a_{H_EC}=V(v_{E,C})a_{H_EC}=a_CUT(v_{E,C}).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $v_{M,VC}$. Every equation holds for each $C$ and uses natural transformations, hence proves the asserted equality of natural transformations.

source.place: First sentence: successive coefficient extensions and scalar-associator equation.

proof.text:
For objects $X=(E,C)$ and $Y=(L,D)$, put $t_{X,F}=S_{F/E}(v_{E,C})$ and $t_{Y,F}=S_{F/L}(v_{L,D})$ at a common field $F$. These are isomorphisms. Step 1 and naturality of $v_F$ at an arbitrary rational arrow $h:S_{F/E}C\to S_{F/L}D$ give
$$\beta_{F/L,D}^{-1}H_F(h)\beta_{F/E,C}=t_{Y,F}^{-1}v_{F,S_{F/L}D}H_F(h)u_{F,S_{F/E}C}t_{X,F}=t_{Y,F}^{-1}h\,t_{X,F}.$$
The middle equality uses $v_{F,S_{F/L}D}H_F(h)=h v_{F,S_{F/E}C}$ and cancels $v_Fu_F$. In particular this uses naturality on all rational arrows, not only arrows lifted integrally.

source.place: First sentence: common-field representative formula and rational naturality.

proof.text:
For $F\subseteq G$ let $W=S_{G/F}$ and $a_X:WS_{F/E}C\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{G/E}C$ be the scalar associator, and similarly $a_Y$. The transition of a representative is $h_G=a_YW(h)a_X^{-1}$. Use $a_{HX}:WS_{F/E}H_EC\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{G/E}H_EC$ for the associator at $H_EC$, and similarly $a_{HY}$. Naturality of the scalar associators at $v_E,v_L$ gives $t_{X,G}a_{HX}=a_XW(t_{X,F})$ and $t_{Y,G}a_{HY}=a_YW(t_{Y,F})$. Therefore
$$a_{HY}W(t_{Y,F}^{-1}h t_{X,F})a_{HX}^{-1}=t_{Y,G}^{-1}a_YW(h)a_X^{-1}t_{X,G}=t_{Y,G}^{-1}h_Gt_{X,G}.$$
This proves compatibility with every transition. Equal representatives agree at a further common field by the definition of the Hom colimit; applying this equality there proves independence of representatives and of the common field. In Lean this is the already proved StageSystem.Morphism.tr_mapAt, after constructing the stage-system morphism with the associator equation of Step 3.

source.place: First sentence: independence of common-field representatives under further extension.

proof.text: Compute identities and composites at one common field, as in the definition of the common-stage category. For an identity the formula of Step 4 is $t_X^{-1}1t_X=1$. For composable $h:X_F\to Y_F$ and $g:Y_F\to Z_F$ it gives $(t_Z^{-1}g t_Y)(t_Y^{-1}h t_X)=t_Z^{-1}gh t_X$. Step 5 permits moving any two initial representatives to this field. Thus the stated object and arrow formulas define a functor. Its object at $(E,C)$ is $(E,H_EC)$, exactly the identity compact-support object in the compact-support definition by the identification in Step 1; its arrows are obtained from that finite-stage functor by its specified coefficient comparisons, as required. Use the existing proved StageSystem.Morphism.functor and functor_map_mkHom: no new pair-category construction or existence axiom is needed.

source.place: First sentence: the actual common-stage identity compact-support functor.

proof.text: Let $v_X=[E,v_{E,C}]$. Its representative at $F$ is exactly $t_{X,F}$; the analogous component $[E,u_{E,C}]$ extends to $t_{X,F}^{-1}$. Their two composites are identities already over $E$. For any $[F,h]:X\to Y$, Step 4 gives $t_{Y,F}(\beta_{F/L,D}^{-1}H_F(h)\beta_{F/E,C})=h t_{X,F}$, proving naturality of $v$ with the specified formula. Before cancelling the $\beta$ this is exactly $v_{F,S_{F/L}D}H_F(h)=h v_{F,S_{F/E}C}$. Step 5 proves preservation by every further extension. Hence these components give the stated natural isomorphism and its stated inverse, without selecting a common field globally or detecting maps by finite reductions. Package the inverse-unit and unit families as Morphism.Hom to and from Morphism.id; their compatibility is the inverse-unit equation and its cancellation. The proved descNatIso and functorIdIso produce v with exactly the required inclusion components.
